concepts.title: The Solar System
concepts.definition: The solar system is the Sun and the family of eight planets, their moons, and other bodies that move around the Sun held by its gravity.
concepts.key_idea: The Sun is at the centre, and eight planets orbit around it in fixed paths called orbits.
question_patterns: What is the solar system?
How many planets are there in the solar system?
What holds the planets in orbit around the Sun?
Name the planets in order from the Sun.
What is an orbit?

solution_steps.explain: The Sun is at the centre of the solar system.
Eight planets -- Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune -- orbit the Sun.
Each planet moves around the Sun in a fixed path called an orbit, held by the Sun's gravity.

worked_examples.answer: The Sun's gravity.

concepts.title: The Sun
concepts.definition: The Sun is a huge ball of hot, glowing gases at the centre of the solar system that gives us light and heat and holds all the planets in orbit.
concepts.key_idea: The Sun is a star that produces its own light and heat and is the main source of energy for Earth.
question_patterns: What is the Sun?
Why is the Sun important for life on Earth?
Is the Sun a planet or a star?
How does the Sun hold the planets in orbit?
Give one example of energy we get from the Sun.

solution_steps.explain: The Sun is a huge ball of hot glowing gases at the centre of the solar system.
It is a star that makes its own light and heat and is the main source of energy for Earth.
The Sun's strong gravity holds all the planets in their orbits.

concepts.title: Planets of the Solar System
concepts.definition: Planets are large, round bodies that orbit the Sun and do not produce their own light; the eight planets differ in size, distance from the Sun, and surface.
concepts.key_idea: The first four planets are small and rocky, while the next four are large and made mostly of gases.
question_patterns: Name the eight planets in order from the Sun.
Which planets are called inner or rocky planets?
Which planets are called outer or gas planets?
Which is the largest planet?
Which planet is known as the Red Planet?

solution_steps.explain: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.
The first four -- Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars -- are small rocky planets; the next four are large gas planets.
Jupiter is the largest and Mars is called the Red Planet.

concepts.title: Counting the Planets
concepts.definition: We can find how many planets lie between two given planets by counting their positions in the order from the Sun.
concepts.key_idea: Subtract the position numbers and take away one to count the planets strictly in between.
question_patterns: How many planets lie between Earth and Jupiter?
Count the planets between Mercury and Mars.
How many planets are between Venus and Saturn?
Find the number of planets between Earth and Neptune.
How many planets lie between Mars and Uranus?

solution_steps.explain: Number the planets from the Sun: Mercury 1, Venus 2, Earth 3, Mars 4, Jupiter 5, Saturn 6, Uranus 7, Neptune 8.
Take the larger position number minus the smaller one.

solution_steps.action: Subtract one for the count between
solution_steps.explain: The planets strictly in between are diff minus one.

worked_examples.question: How many planets lie between Earth (3) and Jupiter (5)?
worked_examples.solution: Subtract the positions: 5 - 3 = 2, then subtract one: 2 - 1 = 1. Only Mars lies between.
worked_examples.answer: 1 planet (Mars).

worked_examples.question: Count the planets between Mercury (1) and Mars (4).
worked_examples.solution: Subtract: 4 - 1 = 3, then subtract one: 3 - 1 = 2. Venus and Earth lie between.
worked_examples.answer: 2 planets (Venus and Earth).

exercises.question: How many planets lie between Venus (2) and Saturn (6)?

concepts.title: Earth in the Solar System
concepts.definition: Earth is the third planet from the Sun and the only known planet that supports life, with air, water, and a suitable temperature.
concepts.key_idea: Earth has air, water, and the right distance from the Sun, making it a unique planet where life can exist.
question_patterns: Why is Earth called a unique planet?
What makes Earth suitable for life?
Which planet is third from the Sun?
Why can life not survive on other planets easily?
Give one reason Earth is special compared to other planets.

solution_steps.explain: Earth is the third planet from the Sun.
Earth has air with oxygen, liquid water, and a comfortable temperature.
These conditions are not found together on other planets, so Earth is the only known planet that supports life.

concepts.title: Stars and Constellations
concepts.definition: Stars are huge balls of hot glowing gases that make their own light, and a constellation is a group of stars that forms a recognisable pattern in the sky.
concepts.key_idea: Stars are very far away and appear tiny; groups of stars form patterns called constellations that help people find their way.
question_patterns: What is a star?
Why do stars appear so small?
What is a constellation?
Name one well-known constellation.
How did people use constellations in the past?

solution_steps.explain: A star is a huge ball of hot glowing gases that makes its own light.
Stars are very far from Earth, so they appear as tiny points of light.
A constellation is a group of stars forming a pattern, such as the Big Dipper or Orion, used to find directions.

concepts.title: Satellites -- Natural and Artificial
concepts.definition: A satellite is a body that moves around a planet; natural satellites like the Moon form naturally, while artificial satellites are made by humans for communication and weather study.
concepts.key_idea: The Moon is a natural satellite, while human-made satellites help in weather forecasting, communication, and studying space.
question_patterns: What is a satellite?
What is the difference between a natural and an artificial satellite?
Give one use of an artificial satellite.
Is the Moon a natural or artificial satellite?
How do artificial satellites help us?

solution_steps.explain: A satellite is any body that orbits a planet.
Natural satellites form in nature, like the Moon; artificial satellites are made by humans.
They help in weather forecasting, television and phone signals, and studying space.

concepts.title: Comets, Asteroids, and Meteors
concepts.definition: Comets are icy bodies with glowing tails, asteroids are small rocky bodies mostly found between Mars and Jupiter, and meteors are small pieces of rock that burn up as shooting stars in the sky.
concepts.key_idea: Besides planets and moons, the solar system has many smaller bodies -- comets, asteroids, and meteors -- moving in space.
question_patterns: What is a comet?
Where are most asteroids found?
What is a meteor or shooting star?
How is a comet different from a planet?
Give one example of a famous comet.

solution_steps.explain: Comets are icy bodies that develop glowing tails when they come near the Sun.
Asteroids are small rocky bodies found mostly in a belt between Mars and Jupiter.
Meteors are small rocks that burn up as bright streaks called shooting stars when they enter Earth's atmosphere.

concepts.title: Telescopes and Space Exploration
concepts.definition: A telescope is an instrument that makes distant objects look closer and is used to study stars and planets; space exploration uses rockets and probes to learn about space.
concepts.key_idea: Telescopes let us see far into space, and spacecraft help humans explore the Moon, planets, and beyond.
question_patterns: What is a telescope?
How does a telescope help us study space?
Name one Indian spacecraft or mission.
Why do scientists send probes into space?
Give one example of what we learned from space exploration.

solution_steps.explain: A telescope is an instrument that gathers light to make distant objects appear closer and clearer.
Scientists use rockets, satellites, and probes to study the Moon, planets, and stars.
India's Chandrayaan mission explored the Moon, and telescopes help us see distant stars and planets.
